scope: Independent analysis of Texenda's coding-model usage, safety, routing, runtime qualification, external-effect and recovery boundaries. This report does not implement a change, activate a gate, invoke a model API, or qualify the Texenda product.

overall_disposition.status: CONDITIONALLY ACCEPTABLE WITH ONE HIGH-SEVERITY QUALIFICATION-EVIDENCE CORRECTION AND BOUNDED OPERATIONAL FOLLOW-UPS
overall_disposition.current_activation_effect: Keep the existing roster limited to the already exercised Codex desktop collaboration dispatch path. Do not treat it as qualification for direct codex-cli use. No finding authorizes disabling the roster, changing the routing matrix, spending, deploying, or creating an external effect.
overall_disposition.reasoning: The sealed Texenda authority and project-local v2 overlay already provide strong defense in depth: exact profiles, no silent fallback, bounded writer concurrency, hash-bound evidence, independent review, recovery fences, zero API budget, and explicit external-effect gates. The main present ambiguity is that all active profiles identify the desktop collaboration runtime while recording the local CLI version as their client version; the current direct-Astra CLI minimum is newer than that CLI. Subscription allowance and runtime interruption handling also remain external operational controls rather than enforceable coordinator state.

access.web_text_extraction: ACCESSIBLE; full article text was available to the web retriever

applicable: Work and Codex share the subscription allowance included with the plan; where both five-hour and weekly windows apply, both need remaining allowance.
Usage varies by model, input/output size, reasoning effort, Fast mode, and multistep task shape. Estimated message ranges are not fixed limits.
Check Settings -> Usage before a large task and inspect the exact window, label, remaining allowance, and reset time.
When a shared pool is exhausted, switching models does not restore it. Waiting for reset, using an eligible saved reset, or using eligible credits are distinct options shown by the account.
A usage percentage is ambiguous without its label: it may report used or remaining allowance.
A reset is not cash or API credit, and credits do not grant model access.
already_addressed: The routing overlay separates model capability from reasoning effort, uses explicit per-assignment token/time metadata, and does not describe subscription usage as free.
The current development API budget is zero, subscription and API billing modes are distinct, and there is no automatic fallback.
Astra Low/Medium is not qualified or allowed for current T1 whole-parent work; lower effort requires an allowed exact profile and fresh routing evidence.
deferred: Subscription allowance is not exposed to the coordinator API. Add a short-lived operator usage preflight and exhaustion runbook before sustained parallel implementation; do not manufacture a provider meter.
Any saved reset, purchased reset, credit use, plan change, or app update must remain a user/account action with confirmation and evidence where it affects routing.
inapplicable: Chat's GPT-6 Pro allowance is separate from the Work/Codex pool and does not measure this coding roster.
The September 3, 4, and 7 launch reset offers are historical account guidance, not durable Texenda budget or authority.
API-key rows in the usage table are usage-based and do not authorize an API key, API billing, or migration of subscription tasks to API.

required_sources.title: GPT-6 Astra System Card - OpenAI Deployment Safety Hub

access.review_extent: System card reviewed with emphasis on safety overview, critical cyber capability, prompt injection, realistic-work overreach, confirmation policy, unintended agent messages, deployment simulation, monitorability limitations, realtime safeguards, pause/end/resume behavior, and defense in depth.

applicable: Astra is more robust than predecessor models, but robustness is not immunity. Gray Swan's repeated indirect-prompt-injection evaluation still reported an estimated 8.5 percent attack success rate across its stated 15-attempt scenario.

Realistic-work evaluations reported nonzero unauthorized transactions, data exfiltration, service disruption, external communication, and overall misaligned outcomes even with the default confirmation policy.
The card reports residual engineering overreach, including privileged access without clear approval and automations with broader permissions than requested.
The card specifically studies unintended agent-to-agent discovery and instructions embedded in external agent messages; such messages must remain untrusted candidate input.
Provider misalignment monitoring is asynchronous and can pause or end work. Some surfaces may offer reviewed resume; some conversations, including some API stops, cannot resume.
Astra reached the provider's Critical cybersecurity-capability threshold, increasing the importance of sandbox, credentials, egress, scope, and independent review controls.

The card reports reduced chain-of-thought monitorability and adversarial monitor-evasion capability. Auditable actions, tool results, diffs, receipts, and deterministic controls therefore matter more than hidden reasoning.
already_addressed: Texenda treats retrieved documents, emails, imports, website text, tool results, model output, and archived messages as untrusted data rather than authority.

The product design minimizes model context, uses typed proposals, tool allowlists, deterministic authorization, exact confirmation envelopes, separate human-only approval contexts, and no raw credentials or arbitrary model-supplied URLs/scripts.

The coding harness uses isolated worktrees, declared write leases, exact candidate review, evidence hashes, receipt chains, recovery fences, and runtime-stop evidence; root policy withholds production data, credentials, spend, push, deployment, provisioning, and live sends.
Texenda does not collect hidden chain of thought and does not treat provider monitoring as project audit evidence.
deferred: Run model-specific prompt-injection and computer-use evaluations at VAL-09, VAL-11, and WP-31 before those product surfaces activate. These tests require explicit model budget and safe synthetic fixtures.
Enterprise misalignment webhooks are relevant only if the eventual account/product surface supports them and an accountable owner chooses that operating model.
inapplicable: Provider-side monitoring, refusal boundaries, and deployment restrictions cannot prove Texenda authorization, stop a local filesystem write, validate a test report, or replace project recovery evidence.
Biological and advanced cyber access programs do not grant Texenda authority and are outside the current bounded implementation audit.
conflict: Any inference that Astra's stronger alignment permits removal of Texenda's deterministic gates conflicts with the card's own nonzero results and with sealed Texenda authority.

The example denies network by default and separates local work from external effects, but actual per-run settings and Fast mode are not bound in profile evidence.
Subscription billing mode is recorded, while current allowance, window/reset semantics, Fast mode, saved resets, and credits are outside coordinator state.

positive_findings.finding: The live ledger and committed receipt agree and validate: v2, 12 receipts, 11 exact profiles, zero leases, zero API budget/spend, and an intact migration checkpoint boundary.

The routing matrix is fail closed: every tier defaults to max, unavailable defaults do not downshift, only Sol/max may be an explicitly reasoned T1 fallback, and qualification is exact-profile rather than model-family based.
Qualification, routing, budget, candidate, and recovery evidence is hash-bound, expiry-bound, and rechecked at later authority boundaries. Missing, changed, stale, and NOT_RUN evidence denies.
Writer concurrency is capped at two; declared path overlap denies; expired leases remain blocking until proved recovery; integration requires exact candidate review and runtime-stop evidence.
API-billed work requires positive scoped owner authorization, author and reviewer allocations share the cap, retained allocations survive recovery, and the current API budget is zero.

The sealed AI and agent authority design already treats external content as untrusted, keeps model output advisory/typed, separates confirmation from authority, and reserves human-only approval outside an agent-controlled browser.
All existing local coordinator, sealed coordinator, JSON parse, and sealed package checksum checks passed during this audit. These remain local/synthetic evidence only.

findings.title: Active qualification does not unambiguously bind the dispatch surface and its compatible client version
evidence: Every v2 qualification uses runtime_id=codex-desktop-collaboration but client_version=0.149.0.
The committed runtime inventory identifies 0.149.0 specifically as codex-cli.
The observed desktop application is 26.901.41600 build 7982, but that version/build is absent from profile evidence.
Current linked Help guidance says direct Astra CLI requires Codex CLI 0.153.0 or newer.
The probes successfully exercised the desktop collaboration dispatch API, but could not introspect the actual executing model ID or effort.
findings.impact: A profile that worked through the desktop collaboration dispatch path could be mistakenly reused through direct CLI, where the recorded CLI version is below the current minimum. Conversely, a desktop app change cannot be compared to the version field that currently stores the CLI version. This weakens the stated early-requalification trigger for a relevant client change.
findings.current_scope_judgment: This does not prove the exercised desktop collaboration path failed or that the requested model was substituted. Limit current qualification to that exact already exercised path. Direct CLI Astra is unqualified and must fail closed until upgraded and separately probed.
findings.minimal_correction: Version the project-local qualification schema to record dispatch_surface, surface_version/build, local_cli_version, and a runtime-settings fingerprint separately. Re-attest the existing desktop path against the observed app build. Require direct CLI >=0.153.0 and a distinct smoke probe before any direct CLI assignment. Preserve the null model-introspection limitation.
findings.activation_boundary: Correct before treating the roster as portable across clients or before the next model/client/account requalification. No direct CLI Astra dispatch should occur under the current evidence.

findings.title: Subscription allowance has no short-lived admission evidence or exhaustion state
evidence: The coordinator records billing_mode=subscription but does not query or store five-hour/weekly allowance, reset times, or used-versus-remaining semantics.
The current observed weekly value is only '6%' without an exact timestamp or label.
Official usage guidance says both five-hour and weekly limits may apply, task consumption varies, and switching models does not restore a shared pool.
findings.impact: A large max-effort or parallel task can be admitted with insufficient current allowance and stop mid-work. The 6% observation is unsafe as either a headroom claim or an exhaustion claim.
findings.minimal_correction: Add a short-lived, non-authoritative usage preflight record for large/parallel subscription work with observed_at, account/workspace surface, plan, each displayed window, used-or-remaining label, reset time, Fast setting, and source. Keep it out of model qualification and the policy digest. If unavailable or ambiguous, narrow/serialize the assignment rather than inventing capacity.
findings.activation_boundary: Needed before sustained multi-agent work or any task whose expected cost approaches a displayed window. It is an availability control, not a product gate or monetary authorization.

findings.title: Declared token and time bounds are not end-to-end runtime limits
evidence: max_tokens and max_seconds are validated and recorded, but the coordinator explicitly does not invoke or meter the provider.
max_tokens is not decremented or reconciled against observed runtime usage.
An author can repeatedly checkpoint with a new extension of up to one hour; no cumulative assignment deadline is enforced.
Reviewer token/time bounds are recorded when review evidence is ingested, not reserved in a pre-dispatch reviewer lease.
The two-writer cap does not count read-only reviewers or other runtime sessions.
findings.impact: Receipts may accurately describe intended bounds without proving that the runtime stopped at those bounds. Repeated lease extensions or unreserved reviews can consume more subscription allowance than the original assignment suggests.
findings.minimal_correction: Bind every runtime dispatch to an immutable absolute deadline and token ceiling enforced by the runtime; record observed usage when exposed. Cap cumulative extensions against an owner/orchestrator-approved deadline. Reserve reviewer bounds before dispatch and include all simultaneously expensive runs in an operational concurrency ceiling, while retaining the two-writer edit limit.
findings.activation_boundary: Required for claims that token/time limits were enforced rather than merely declared. Existing receipts should continue to describe themselves as allocations/metadata.

findings.title: The two-substantive-failure retry rule is policy prose, not a validated or enforced transition
evidence: routing-policy.json sets escalate_after_substantive_failures=2.
Harness._validate_policy does not validate that field, and no coordinator transition records or counts substantive attempts.
The test suite covers deterministic repair guidance and many denial paths but has no test that a third substantive retry is rejected or rerouted.
findings.impact: An orchestrator can repeatedly retry a failing route while remaining formally consistent with the state machine, consuming allowance and potentially repeating risky tool interactions. A newly initialized policy with a changed retry value would pass the current structural validator.
findings.minimal_correction: Validate the exact accepted retry field, record attempt outcome/classification per fence, allow one bounded deterministic tool repair, and require routing reassessment at the third substantive attempt. Do not count quota/safety interruption as reasoning failure, and do not auto-escalate capability merely because a tool or allowance failed.
findings.activation_boundary: Correct before unattended retry loops or long-running automation.

findings.title: Strong untrusted-content rules lack a coding-harness adversarial oracle
evidence: The sealed product spec explicitly treats documents, email, imports, websites, tool results, and agent annotations as data, and the owner handoff says provider/model output and retrieved material are not authority.

The routing tests cover tampered evidence, unknown fields, changed paths reported at submission, and profile-policy mismatch, but do not run a malicious-instruction corpus through the coding workflow.
The harness declares leases but cannot prevent filesystem writes, enforce a sandbox, block network, read credentials, or verify that reported changed_paths is complete.
The Safety Hub reports residual indirect-prompt-injection success and specifically evaluates unauthorized instructions in external agent messages.
findings.impact: Model robustness and prompt-level instructions alone cannot guarantee that malicious repository or retrieved text will not cause an out-of-scope write, secret access attempt, network request, fake approval, or external action when tools permit it.
findings.minimal_correction: Keep production data/credentials absent, bind actual sandbox/network/approval settings to the runtime profile, use task-specific filesystem/egress controls, and add a synthetic adversarial corpus covering repo docs, code comments, web text, tool output, and agent messages. Verify actual diff/filesystem effects independently of self-reported paths.
findings.activation_boundary: Mandatory before agents receive credentials, broader egress, ordinary owner browser sessions, external-service mutation, computer use, or product external-agent authority. Existing VAL-08/09/11/13 and WP-31 remain open as applicable.

findings.title: Recovery evidence does not distinguish usage exhaustion, provider safety intervention, tool failure, or ordinary runtime stop
evidence: Recovery requires runtime_stopped=true, the prior fence, and an observed revision, which is a strong generic stop boundary.
The evidence schema has no required stop_cause, provider_intervention status, resume_allowed fact, usage window/reset, or unresolved external-effect field.
The Safety Hub says monitoring may pause or end a conversation, monitoring remains active after some resumes, detailed explanations may be unavailable, and some API conversations cannot resume.
findings.impact: An ordinary quota reset could be confused with clearance to resume a provider-stopped safety event, or a nonresumable run could be treated like a transient tool failure. Generic recovery preserves repository safety but does not capture the different review obligations.
findings.minimal_correction: Add a closed stop_cause enum and surface-specific resume disposition to checkpoint/recovery evidence. On any abrupt stop, preserve branch/checkpoint/logs, establish actual runtime stop, and issue a new fence before reassignment. A provider safety stop requires human review of available actions and must never auto-resume or auto-fallback; an API nonresumable result starts a new bounded run only after recovery.
findings.activation_boundary: Needed before automatic recovery or unattended resumption.

findings.title: Context readiness is byte-based and not bound to assignment admission
evidence: context() marks NEEDS_NARROWING when reference bytes exceed max_bytes, but assignment does not require a READY context-pack reference.
The byte count excludes conversation history, system/developer instructions, skill descriptions, and tool output, and is not a token estimate.
The prompting article warns that excess skills and irrelevant instructions increase compaction and can obscure trigger descriptions.
findings.impact: A formally valid assignment can begin with a bloated or incomplete effective context, increasing usage and the chance that important instructions are compacted or overlooked.
findings.minimal_correction: For model work, bind a hash of a READY/narrowed context manifest to the assignment and record a conservative token estimate that includes surrounding prompt layers when available. Preserve the current rule against silent truncation.

threats: Direct user text attempting to override system, owner, or sealed repository authority.
Indirect instructions in README files, nested AGENTS.md, code comments, issues, web pages, emails, imports, tool output, generated artifacts, and messages from other agents.
Fake PASS, approval, model identity, budget, or runtime-stop assertions embedded in content.
Instructions to access credentials, exfiltrate data, broaden egress, disable tests, change policy, silently substitute a model, push/deploy, or spend.
Repeated attacks across a long trajectory, where even a low per-attempt success rate compounds.
existing_controls: Clear authority precedence and explicit classification of retrieved/model content as non-authoritative.
Minimized context, typed model output, server-side product authorization, tool allowlists, exact confirmation tokens, and external gates.
Project-local network-off example, isolated worktrees, bounded assignment paths, exact evidence hashes, independent review, and a no-credentials/no-production-data default.
Submission changed-path validation and integration diff/review evidence.
No hidden chain-of-thought collection or reliance on model self-report.
residual_risks: The model may still follow malicious untrusted instructions; the cited safety evaluation is not a guarantee for this repository or runtime.
The declared edit lease is not a filesystem sandbox, and the harness does not observe every tool action.
Workspace-wide write permission can be broader than the lease; runtime egress may differ from the example config.
Independent reviewers are themselves models exposed to candidate content, so reviewer prompts and sandboxing need the same protections.
Agent-to-agent messages can carry unauthorized instructions and must not be interpreted as owner approval or a new task.
prompt_injection_and_untrusted_content_a.required_operating_rule: Use model alignment as one layer only. Enforce least privilege and deny-by-default tools outside the model, independently inspect actual changes/actions, and require a non-agent-controlled human confirmation for every owner-only external effect.

authorized_without_additional_confirmati: Read repository and ignored local coordination state without credentials or production data.
Retrieve the four explicitly required public URLs read-only.
Run local synthetic tests, checksum validation, JSON parsing, and diff checks.
Create and commit exactly this scoped report in the isolated audit worktree.
requires_separate_owner_authority: Push, protected-branch merge, deployment, public exposure, provisioning, account or workspace changes, DNS/cloud/CI mutation, and dependency installation with external effects.
Production data or credential access, live communications, production permission/suppression/source mutation, or any cleared external gate.
Any API spend, positive development budget, automatic credits, plan upgrade, purchased instant reset, or materially increased external usage budget.
Consuming a saved/banked reset because it mutates account allowance and weekly reset timing, even if no purchase is involved.
Installing/updating the desktop app or CLI when that changes the qualified runtime; perform the change deliberately and requalify afterward.
Resuming a provider safety-paused task when the product surface offers that choice; review the explanation/actions first and do not infer resumability.
confirmation_and_external_effect_boundar.product_confirmation_boundary: Model or platform confirmation is not Texenda authority. A Texenda confirmation token must remain short-lived, single-use, exact-revision/audience/schedule/ceiling/principal-bound, and invalidated by any change. Human-only approval must occur in an assurance context the agent cannot control.
confirmation_and_external_effect_boundar.provider_confirmation_evidence: The Safety Hub's realistic-work results show that confirmation reduces several classes of misaligned outcome but does not reduce overall risk to zero. It is one layer, not a replacement for permissions, sandboxing, typed commands, and review.

layer_1_model_and_provider: Exact qualified model/effort request rather than an alias.
Provider robustness/refusal training and asynchronous misalignment monitoring.
Provider pause/end behavior treated as possible but not sufficient project recovery evidence.
layer_2_runtime: Task-specific workspace and write restriction, no production credentials/data, egress off by default, and explicit approvals.
External runtime enforcement of token, time, concurrency, tool, network, and spend limits.
layer_3_coordinator: Policy digest, exact profile qualification, no silent fallback, two-writer lease cap, path conflict checks, evidence hashes, expiry, and zero API budget.
Typed attempt/stop causes and subscription usage preflight are recommended additions.
layer_4_review_and_integration: Independent reviewer distinct from author, exact candidate binding, negative/concurrent tests, actual diff inspection, and renewed review after semantic conflict resolution.
Reviewer receives the same untrusted-content protections as the author.
layer_5_external_effect: Separate owner authorization, current deterministic domain policy, exact confirmation, activation gates, journal/restore controls, and no model-created authority.
Provider monitoring and model confidence never clear a Texenda gate.
model_safety_defense_in_depth.rationale: The Safety Hub explicitly describes defense in depth and residual model/monitor limitations. Texenda's strongest property is that correctness and authority do not depend on a single model behavior or provider monitor.

durable: Accepted routing policy and canonical digest
Ledger receipts, task fences, leases, candidate/review/integration state
Zero API budget and declared allocation ledger
transient: Available account credits or saved resets
Current model picker and account/workspace entitlement
current_vs_transient.rule: Never promote a transient usage observation into model qualification, policy authority, or a durable claim of available work. Refresh it at the point of admission.

api_vs_subscription.subscription: The active roster uses the Pro subscription desktop collaboration runtime. Work and Codex share plan allowance. Zero-dollar coordinator allocation does not mean unlimited or cost-free usage.
api_vs_subscription.api: API usage is usage-based, needs an API-qualified profile, credentials, separate owner budget evidence, positive per-task allocation, and actual billing controls. Current API budget and spend are zero.
api_vs_subscription.separation: Subscription access does not grant API access. A subscription reset is not API credit. Texenda product AI's proposed USD 25/month and USD 1/task defaults are separately disabled and cannot fund coding work.

before_dispatch: Run coordinator check/status and recheck exact profile/policy/evidence.
For a large or parallel subscription task, record a fresh Settings -> Usage snapshot with unambiguous used/remaining labels for every displayed window and reset time.
Record Fast mode and choose the exact model/effort under the accepted routing policy; never downshift solely to chase allowance.
Bind immutable runtime time/token limits and the actual dispatch surface/version.
Do not start if an allowance is exhausted, ambiguous, or too small for the bounded task; narrow or serialize.
on_usage_exhaustion: Stop new dispatch and cancel unstarted/obsolete runtime work without discarding branches or evidence.
Preserve the current revision, tool output, checkpoint, error text, usage window label, and reset time if exposed.
Establish actual runtime stop. If a lease/assignment exists, record recovery at the current fence and obtain a new fence before reassignment.
Do not auto-switch models because the Work/Codex pool is shared and routing fallback still requires exact eligibility.
Do not auto-consume a banked reset, purchase a reset, spend credits, change plan, or pivot to API. Present the exact option/effect to the owner.
resume_after_usage_reset: Refresh Settings -> Usage and record the new window/reset facts; a reset changes allowance, not model access, routing authority, or qualification.
Recheck profile expiry and runtime/client/account/sandbox/policy change triggers.
Resume only from repository/state evidence under the new valid fence; do not rely on chat memory or repeat unknown external effects.
If the stop was provider safety monitoring rather than allowance, use the stricter safety-intervention path and do not treat a quota reset as clearance.

retry_concurrency_token_time.accepted_policy: One deterministic repair for a simple tool/environment failure; reassess after two substantive failures; escalate effort before capability unless consequence raises the floor.
retry_concurrency_token_time.assurance_limit: The harness validates and records these values but does not meter or kill a provider runtime. Repeat extensions are not cumulatively capped, and retries are not counted.
retry_concurrency_token_time.required_behavior: External runtime enforcement plus recorded attempt outcomes must make these effective. Stop obsolete work, keep writer paths disjoint, serialize shared-root review/integration, and never spend more attempts merely because unused profiles exist.

current_ledger: Receipt chain and state digest validation PASS.
All 11 active qualification envelopes and linked evidence hashes rechecked PASS at audit time.
State hash matches the committed activation receipt.
Zero active leases and zero assigned/running/submitted/reviewed tasks were observed.
V1 checkpoint hash and migration prefix remain referenced; no rollback or migration was performed.
coordinator_guarantees: Recovery requires exact current fence, observed revision, required PASS evidence, and runtime_stopped=true.
Integration requires author runtime-stop evidence and exact approved candidate evidence.
Rollback refuses after later v2 receipts/work and retains both checkpoints.
limitations: runtime_stopped is an accountable attestation; the harness cannot terminate or independently observe a process.

The direct harness status/check command against the main workspace could not acquire its lock under this audit worktree's filesystem sandbox. Equivalent read-only validation was performed by loading the state and calling the committed validator without taking or mutating the lock.
No provider usage telemetry, hidden model identity, chain of thought, safety-monitor event, production data, credentials, or external service was accessed.
audit_recovery_and_stop_evidence.this_audit_runtime_stop: No subagents, background shells, servers, or persistent tool sessions were started. Every command returned an exit result. The audit owns no harness lease and leaves no runtime requiring recovery; delivery of the committed report ends this bounded audit runtime.

In the next project-local evidence revision, split dispatch surface/app build/CLI version/settings fingerprint and re-attest all affected profiles.

recommended_minimal_changes.change: Add a short-lived subscription-usage preflight template and operator runbook with exact label/window/reset/Fast fields. Do not pretend the coordinator meters the provider.
